title: Sigma schedules: where the steps go

options: The list of noise levels the sampler will visit
questions.answer: The list of noise levels the sampler will visit
questions.why: calculate_sigmas in comfy/samplers.py returns that list, ending at 0.

questions.q: Karras et al. found ρ = 3 nearly equalises per-step truncation error. Why use ρ = 7?
options: It is required by the ODE
ρ between 5 and 10 gave better images, which suggests errors near σ_min matter a lot
questions.answer: ρ between 5 and 10 gave better images, which suggests errors near σ_min matter a lot
questions.why: Stated in their section 3. The value comes from experiment on images.

questions.q: What does a flow shift above 1 do?
options: Spends more of the steps at high noise
Spends more steps at low noise
questions.answer: Spends more of the steps at high noise
questions.why: The lab shows shift 3 at 8 steps: 1.000, 0.955, 0.900, against 1.000, 0.875, 0.750 for shift 1.

questions.q: In the lab, what does `normal` at 10 steps with DPM++ 2M show?
options: normal is always the worst schedule
The best schedule depends on the solver: normal is fine with Euler but far worse with DPM++ 2M here
questions.answer: The best schedule depends on the solver: normal is fine with Euler but far worse with DPM++ 2M here
questions.why: Its Euler error is mid-table, while its DPM++ 2M error at 10 steps is six times exponential's.

questions.q: Why does ComfyUI scale the first noise by √(1+σ²) at full denoise?
options: To include the latent's own variance of about 1
Because of the VAE scale factor
questions.answer: To include the latent's own variance of about 1
questions.why: EPS.noise_scaling uses it. With x = x_0 + σε and unit-variance latents, the total variance is 1 + σ².
